source:
Game: Last Rogent (prototype)
Build a simple Roblox tower-defense / wave-survival game. A base sits at the end of a fixed path. Enemies spawn and walk the path toward the base. The player deploys and upgrades AI "agents" that fight the enemies. Survive escalating waves.
Core loop (this is the whole game for now):
 1. Prep - between waves, the player spends orbs (currency) to place or upgrade agents on fixed slots along the path.
 2. Fight - press "Start Wave." Enemies spawn and march the path. Placed agents auto-attack enemies in range. Enemies that reach the base deal damage to base health.
 3. Loot - killed enemies drop orbs. Orb count ticks up on screen.
 4. Repeat for the next, harder wave.
v1 scope - keep it minimal:
 • One agent type: place it on a slot, it auto-shoots the nearest enemy. Upgradable 1→2→3 (more damage / range each level).
 • One enemy type: walks the path, has HP, drops orbs on death, damages the base if it reaches the end.
 • 10 waves, each with more enemies and slightly more HP than the last.
 • Base health (e.g. 20). Hit 0 = game over. Survive wave 10 = win.
 • Simple UI: base health, current orb count, current wave number, and a "Start Wave" button.
Feel: fast, readable, satisfying. Orbs pop out of dead enemies. Placing/upgrading an agent is one tap on a slot. No menus, no accounts, no data saving yet - just the loop working in Play mode.
Start with a flat baseplate, a straight path of parts from a spawn point to the base, agent slots along the path, and get one wave fully working before adding the rest.

answers.ask: No visual theme was given beyond a grey baseplate prototype — should the finished map read as sci-fi, fantasy, or stylized toon?
answers.answer: Use a stylized toon prototype look: clean, colorful, highly readable shapes on the flat baseplate.

scene_prompt: Create a simple stylized-toon tower-defense map on a flat grey baseplate, using clean colorful, highly readable shapes. A straight path made of parts runs from an enemy spawn point at one end to a base at the opposite end. Arrange fixed agent placement slots at intervals along both sides of the path, with open space around them for clear visibility; the base is the path endpoint.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is Strategy, specifically a tower-defense wave-survival prototype: hostile waves follow one fixed route toward a defended base.

### Shape and preset
Use `lane-actor-track`, the Tower Defense preset. Here it is a single straight, unbranching ground-level lane from the enemy end of the baseplate to the base at the other end. The preset remains recognisable, retaining the dedicated track, defense placement ground, base, and enemy origin; omit its pinch point because the prompt specifies a straight readable path.

### Config requirements
Use `buildzone-grid` as evenly spaced fixed agent-slot pads running along both sides of the path, with broad clear ground around every pad. Use `tracker-core` as the colorful defended base structure visibly terminating the path.

### Layout requirements
Use `tracker-core` with one base-health target located at the exact endpoint of the straight path. Use `spawner-npc` with one hostile-wave origin placed at the opposite path endpoint, facing directly down the lane toward the base. No pickups, checkpoints, or additional placed triggers are required by the stated map space.

### Layout components
Build one small flat grey baseplate as the complete map. Place the enemy-spawn zone at one narrow end and the base at the far end. A straight path of modular parts crosses the baseplate between them with no branches, crossings, turns, or obstacles. Flank the full length of this route with regularly spaced fixed agent placement pads on both sides, leaving open sightlines and generous visibility around the pads and lane. The surrounding terrain remains flat grey prototype ground, with the colorful path, slot pads, spawn marker, and base as the only strong visual landmarks. The boundary is the outer edge of the baseplate. Frame the entire lane end-to-end in an elevated three-quarter isometric composition, clearly showing the spawn-to-base direction and both rows of slots.

### Render order
Use `authored_plan`: the fixed enemy lane must be valid by construction as one continuous, unbroken route from spawn to core before it is dressed.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is small, driven by one compact lane, one base, one spawn, and a limited set of defense slots. Theme is a stylized toon prototype: clean colorful shapes against a neutral grey baseplate, with maximum route readability. Apply `P6` because the tower-defense track must remain a valid continuous enemy path.
